extracted.intended_audience: researchers, potential proposers, program managers, and other stakeholders interested in DARPA research programs and solicitations
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding criteria and site-level guidance describing what DARPA programs are designed to achieve (their goals, structure, and scope) and how users should find programs on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand the definition of what’s possible
rubrics_metrics.description: By design, our programs expand the definition of what’s possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are intended to push boundaries and extend what can be achieved technologically; they are deliberately ambitious in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite duration with lasting change
rubrics_metrics.description: Their duration is finite, but they create lasting change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are time-limited efforts (not open-ended) but are expected to have persistent impact beyond their active period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managed by technical offices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are run under DARPA's technical offices, indicating domain-aligned technical oversight and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Span laboratory, applied sciences, and advanced engineering disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: DARPA programs span the laboratory and applied sciences and advanced engineering disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program content may range from fundamental lab research to applied engineering work across multiple disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typically structured in phases
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program execution commonly follows phased development (e.g., exploratory, development, transition), reflecting staged progress toward goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tackle urgent national security challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Each program tackles an urgent national security challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program objectives are focused on pressing national security needs rather than purely academic curiosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solution must have potential for strategic technological surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Solution whose solution has the potential to achieve strategic technological surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferred program outcomes are those that could produce unexpected, game-changing technological advantages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue trusted, disruptive capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each program embodies our quest for trusted, disruptive capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs aim to produce capabilities that are both disruptive (novel, high-impact) and trusted (reliable, usable in operational contexts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revolutionize the state of the art
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs seek to revolutionize the state of the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond incremental improvement, programs should aim to transform current technological baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and discovery guidance for programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the filters to narrow results by research topic or office. Check both Current and Completed programs. Search by keyword for your specific programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site-specific procedural guidance for finding programs: apply topic/office filters, include both current and completed listings when relevant, and use keyword search to locate specific programs of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site resources and listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources: Challenges, Ideas under incubation, Research spotlights, RSS feed for Opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site provides related resources and feeds (challenges, incubating ideas, spotlights, and an RSS for opportunities) to learn about and track program activity and opportunities.
